decision: tagged a-better-me master as powersync-final before any change
why: a rollback point for the app, its data stays in Supabase untouched

decision: definition of done: a-better-me on master syncs through sync-engine with no PowerSync, Postgres, Hyperdrive or Docker; two simulators converge within 2 s online; a write made while the server is down lands after it returns; CI green; Worker deployed; production rows imported and counted equal; a device against production shows them
why: a falsifiable predicate before building anything

decision: rigor high: production import verified by row counts and a device, merge is the deploy, tag is the rollback
why: merging a-better-me master deploys the Worker, so the merge is the one-way door

decision: writes are captured by generated per-table SQLite triggers into an _outbox that stores no values; the push reads current rows
why: no client code can forget to queue a change, the same DDL serves TypeScript and Swift, and five offline edits to one column send one value

decision: schema evolution is additive only, computed from PRAGMA table_info on both sides; no schema hash or shape version in v1
why: a-better-me already states every new column is nullable or defaulted, and a hash would only add a reset path nothing needs yet

decision: one /sync call carries the outbox and the cursor; a pulled row with a pending outbox entry is skipped until its write is acked
why: a pull can never overwrite an edit the server has not seen

decision: two parallel builders in sync-engine worktrees: TypeScript packages and the Swift package, against docs/protocol.md; then a-better-me server and iOS in parallel; architect skill skipped because the shapes are already written down
why: the protocol doc is the contract; a second design round over it would be over-engineering
